title: Scientific LLM Orchestrator authority boundary
text: The Scientific LLM Orchestrator is a research prototype for routing bounded scientific software tasks among frontier, hosted and local workers. Scientific validity, citation acceptance, security severity, canonical-source acceptance and release authority stay with a frontier or human reviewer. Worker routes are proposal lanes and do not automatically apply generated code.

title: Deterministic routing gates
text: The orchestrator's routing layer checks an architecture allowlist, allowed path scope, validation allowlists, automatic-apply prohibition and authority flags before selecting frontier, hosted-worker, local-worker or blocked routes. When preferred workers are unavailable, bounded fallback rules are deterministic.

title: Schema subset validator
text: The project includes a standard-library validator for the exact JSON Schema subset used by the repository. It supports object and scalar types, required properties, properties, additionalProperties, enum, const, pattern, minLength, arrays, items and minItems. The implementation explicitly states that it is not a complete JSON Schema implementation.

title: Human-agent WebMCP control room
text: Captain is a public synthetic WebMCP demonstration in which a browser agent can inspect work items, compare worker routes, focus an item and stage a reversible assignment proposal. Human approval and release are deliberately not exposed as agent tools, preserving visible human authority.

title: Binder-jet monitoring evidence pattern
text: A binder-jet monitoring workflow can compare a designed jetting pattern with a captured bed image, compute match, over-jet and missing-jet regions, and track defect rates layer by layer. A scientifically defensible system must distinguish image-processing metrics from validated closed-loop machine control.

title: Vaterite synthesis evidence pattern
text: A vaterite calcium-carbonate synthesis workflow should record reagent identity, concentration, addition sequence, temperature, mixing conditions, pH and phase-quantification method. Simulation outputs such as speciation or mixing fields should be treated as screening evidence until experimental XRD or other phase measurements validate the final product.

title: Cement clinker scale-up evidence pattern
text: Clinker process development should separate raw-meal design, thermal history, phase quantification and mechanical performance. Pilot-scale agreement with laboratory results is stronger evidence than composition calculations alone, while commercial readiness additionally requires reproducibility, process economics and operating-window evidence.

title: Patent landscaping evidence pattern
text: A patent-landscape workflow should normalize patent families, separate applications from granted rights, track assignees and inventors, compare claims rather than titles alone, and distinguish analyst-created novelty conclusions from source facts. Family normalization prevents duplicate counting of related filings.

title: Scientific RAG grounding rule
text: A scientific RAG answer should expose the evidence identifiers supporting material claims. If retrieval returns only weakly related documents, the system should abstain or state that the evidence is insufficient rather than synthesize an unsupported conclusion.

title: RAG evaluation design
text: Useful retrieval evaluation includes direct fact queries, multi-document synthesis queries, distractor or near-match queries and unsupported queries. Retrieval hit rate and reciprocal rank should be evaluated separately from answer grounding, citation coverage and abstention behavior.

title: Physics-AI claim boundary
text: A Physics-AI digital twin may combine mechanistic simulation with learned surrogates or soft sensors. Planning documents, simulated data and prototype code do not by themselves establish plant-grade accuracy. Validation requires measured data, hold-out conditions, uncertainty analysis and explicit failure boundaries.

title: Engineering deployment evidence hierarchy
text: For engineering AI, a notebook or offline benchmark is weaker evidence than a reproducible service, monitored pilot or user-facing workflow. Production claims should require versioned deployment, latency and failure evidence, observability, rollback or recovery behavior, and real-user or real-process validation where applicable.
